You use modals to make suggestions.
You can also use verbs like recommend and suggest.
The most common modals for making suggestions are: should, could, ought to and had better.
You can think of modals as “helping verbs”. They add meaning to the main verb of a sentence. In this case, these modals add the meaning of advice and suggestion.

Should is the most common modal used to give advice and to make suggestions.
Ought to and had better are used for giving strong advice and making strong suggestions.
You can use the verbs recommend and suggest to make suggestions.

For example:
I recommend starting there.
I recommend that you start there.
I suggest starting there.
I recommend that you start there.
You can also you a question starting with Why don't you/we ...

For example:
Why don't we start from the beginning?

Using the Simple Present, Past and Future Tenses to Plan a Strategy
When you talk about a strategy you can use the present, past and future tenses to explain your ideas.
When you are making a plan for the future you use the simple future.

For example:
This time we will need to make Farmani fully aware of the problem.
To justify or explain your future plans, you can use the simple present.

For example:
I have a few reservations about the issue that we ought to discuss.
You can also use the past tense to show that you are basing your plans on past experience.

For example:
The first crisis came from a direct decision Farmani made.
We have a crisis and I'm worried about what approach I will adopt when confronting Farmani.
I was concerned about the rumor affecting our reputation.
Perhaps you could look at it from a different perspective.

Instructions: Complete the following steps. Fill in the Self-Assessment.

images.text:
Rocco: Ok, so we have a delicate business at hand.
Janet: I called you in because of your discretion.
Rocco: What's the matter?
Janet: We have a crisis and I'm worried about what approach I will adopt when confronting Farmani.
Rocco: Why don't we start from the beginning? I think we should consider planning this carefully.
Janet: It's a good idea. I have a few reservations about the issue that we ought to discuss.
Rocco: Your initial concern wasn't personal. I recommend starting there.
Janet: Alright. First, I was concerned about the rumor affecting our reputation.

Rocco: Right. You managed that first crisis well. Couldn't we use the same approach?
Janet: Sorry, but I don't think it would work. The last crisis was prevention. This one will involve change.
Rocco: I see. Perhaps you could look at it from a different perspective. The first crisis came from a direct decision Farmani made. This time we will need to make Farmani fully aware of the problem.
Janet: I see your point. We had better present the problem directly to him.
Rocco: It's a good idea. It's probably worth acting as if you believe he's entirely innocent. You could always make it look as if you want to help, not accuse him.
Janet: I like it. It might prove effective.

Rocco: Exactly. Then, I suggest you add your personal concern.
Janet: I'm not sure about that.
Rocco: Take it from me, it will soften things if it looks as if you are appealing to his good nature. I have the feeling he will take advantage of this. This will make him want to become a human rights fighter.
